speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Disappointing result, disappointing performance.  So, completely different than I felt after the  
game. Losing twice in a row is something that I  think we do for the first time, but that probably  
also comes with going into the latter stages of  a tournament. So facing Paris Saint-Germain and  
Newcastle in the final are two very good teams,  both in their own styles, but very difficult teams  
to face because we already knew from the game  against St. James’ Park how difficult it is to  
beat them. It was a tough week, but it was also  a week where we extended our lead to 12 points  
from it being 10. So it wasn’t all negative, but  yeah, the last two were definitely not the way  
we wanted it to be. Do you think that it was the  team was physically fatigued or mentally fatigued  
or a combination of both today? After what? Yeah,  mentally it’s always difficult to judge. Were we  
on Tuesday mentally or physically tired? No. But  this game had nothing to do with running. This  
game had only to do with playing duels and there  was no intensity in terms of running in this game  
at all. So you cannot even judge it if we were  tired, yes or no, physically. Because we could  
not press them. You can judge a team if they are  tired and if they press, but there was nothing  
to press because they played over our press. If  they had a goal kick and if they got a free kick,  
which they had quite a lot of in the first half,  they every time brought it into our last line,  
which led to a lot of set pieces. So the game was  slow and not intense, so it’s difficult to judge  
for me if we were physically ready. Mentally, it’s  always, yeah, that’s a difficult one. If you look  
at the result and the performance, you might feel  that it maybe did something to us, but I prefer  
to look at how the game went and this game went  exactly the way they wanted it to be, a fight  
with a lot of duels and a lot of duels through the  air. And if we play 10 times a game of football  
through the air against them, they win it probably  9 times because they are a stronger team through  
the air than us, which led to the first goal and  the second goal because the second goal was also a  
header that they won at the 2nd post that fell for  Isak and led to the two-nil. You told them about  
Jules in the air, correct me if I’m wrong,  but you know more about the same to me. Nah,  
again, credits to Newcastle, but I can explain.  We play zonal, so we have a lot of five players  
zonally close to our goal. So if the ball falls  there, there’s always one of the five stronger  
players that is going to attack that ball. And we  have three players that man-mark and Macca is one  
of them. And normally a player like Dan Burn or  another one runs to the zone because normally,  
and I think he’s an exception to that, I’ve  never seen in my life, a player from that far  
away heading a ball with so much force into  the far corner. So that is part of logic,  
that they either have to go far away from our  zone, which is 99 out of 100 times that will  
never lead to a goal, or they have to arrive  in our zone, and then it’s an equal battle,  
if you want to call it like this. So credit to  him. I think he’s one of the few players that  
can score a goal from that distance with his head.  You mentioned that it’s a wondering performance.  
No, because it’s 70 years since they’ve last won  a trophy, maybe, but that’s for the fans and the  
players want to have 15 years to play football  and they want to win every single trophy they are  
competing for. That’s also what we want, but it  was a game that went the way they wanted it to go.  
And they got just before halftime some extra  energy with the goal, which they probably  
deserved after the first 45 minutes because they  were threatening us more than we threatened them.  
And so, yeah, I don’t think there was more  hunger for them. The game went the way they  
wanted it to go and they are stronger in that part  of football than us, and that’s why they beat us.  
Yeah, you try to make some changes, so you go  to a #9 that’s even stronger for the air than  
or maybe is because you’re hoping that he Darwin  in this situation can make it a bit more difficult  
for their defenders to win all these long balls  we had to play in the first half because I think  
Dan Burn I think he won every duel but and he  played somewhere around 150 no but he played a  
lot. So you try to influence it like this and you  try and you’re showing at halftime that in the few  
moments that are left when the ball is over on  the ground, that we have a bit more time than we  
think and we could make better decisions than we  made in the first half. And that’s also what I saw  
immediately after halftime when we played Fábio  with a triangle and he dribbled all the way in,  
played the ball to Jota and that led to, not to a  chance because Joelinton threw himself in front of  
the ball. But I saw the second half, us playing  through them a bit more, but a bit, not a lot,  
but a bit more. Such a damaging week going out for  Champions League and now losing the major final.  
How do you ensure that does have a knock-on effect  for the rest of the season? Like I said from the  
start, it took us 7, 8, nine months to lose twice  in a row and that happens against two teams that  
are, one of them is fighting for Champions League.  Newcastle is a very good team. We knew this  
already at St. James’ Park and the other one is  Paris Saint-Germain. Probably if you can beat us  
in that style of play, you are probably the best  team in Europe. At the moment, they still have  
to show if they still can beat us in the upcoming  two or three months. But I want to make clear one  
more time that the week started off really well by  us beating Southampton. That’s why we extended our  
lead to 12 points with nine games to go. And yeah,  you know if you go far in tournaments that the  
opposition in your face gets stronger and stronger  and that you can lose even Liverpool can lose  
football games. That’s what can happen. Yeah, we  were outplayed in their style. Yeah, that’s true.  
But that’s yeah, that is what you can call  outplayed. Yeah, they want more duels than us. Is  
that what you mean? Outwork? Is that an outworking  or are they just is that their one of their  
biggest qualities to play so much aerial duels  and to win these physique duels. Outplayed for  
me is if you don’t touch the ball and they play  through you every single time you try to press  
them and every time you’re too late. That is for  me outplayed, but I agree with you if you say that  
they deserved to win because the game went in the  way they wanted it to go. So yes, they deserved  
to win, but it wasn’t like we were only running  after them. We had to defend a lot of long balls,  
second balls, and that’s their strength, yeah.  Last one. Is that a good time for the team to, you  
know, not have a few games on the international,  but considering the two bad results and then,  
you know, what would it take it out? Is it a good  time to maybe have that break? We are here in one  
of the biggest clubs in the world, Liverpool,  but it’s not for the first time in their history  
or in the last two seasons that they’ve lost two  games in a row. This is part of playing football,  
especially if one of them is when you face the  best team in Europe at the moment and the other  
one is facing Newcastle, which is a very strong  team in England. So I would have loved to play  
next week, but now the situation is that they  go to the national teams where they have to play  
two more games again. And then it’s probably 1 1/2  week before we face Everton, which is again a team  
we already faced, and we know how difficult that  one was. So let’s see. I think there are two just,  
that’s the one I ask a question. And the other  one is there. I don’t think physically. Because of  
what I just said, if you looked at how we played  Tuesday, it was the best physical performance in  
my 8 or 9 or 10 months at Liverpool. I’ve never  seen a team working so hard, trying to press the  
other team, so aggressive, running so much. Today,  it wasn’t about running, it was more about duels.  
Yeah, mentally, it’s always tough to lose a final.  It’s always tough if you wear the Liverpool shirt  
to go out of Europe. But again, last season, we, I  think, I’m not sure, quarter-final or last 16 when  
they were when they lost against Atalanta 3-0,  and yeah, it’s part of football if you face strong  
teams that you can lose as well, but ideally you  go through the whole season only winning, winning,  
winning, but but yeah, it can happen that you  also, after 8 months of football, lose twice in  
a row if you face Paris Saint-Germain,  Newcastle. Hold on. Yeah. Thank you.
title: Arne Slot post-match press conference | Liverpool 1-2 Newcastle | Carabao Cup Final
